receiptShapesToReproduce.source: the four receipts the scratchpad closure v3 wrote for U17 on main; the generator must reproduce these key sets key-for-key
receiptShapesToReproduce.conditionalKeys: blobEqualityCheck is added to the merge receipt only under --skip-blob-check; expectedReds and reproofCommit are added to the mainProof receipt only when those flags are given. None of the four receipts on main carries one, which is why they are absent from the key sets above.

designF3.finding: U17 F3: --skip-blob-check turns off the blob-equality comparison of the squash against the PR head over the PR's own files. It is documented as pin-only and the merge receipt records the skip, but nothing stopped a caller from passing it against a real ledger.
designF3.chosen: refuse the flag whenever the RESOLVED ledger directory is the repository's own openspec/planning/2026-09-12-roadmap-completion (DEFAULT_LEDGER_DIR from roadmap-ledger-lib.mjs), whether that is because --ledger-dir was absent or because it named that directory explicitly
designF3.whyNotAnEnvironmentVariable: ROADMAP_LOOP_PIN=1 is set as easily as the flag is passed, so it moves the hole rather than closing it. Binding the weakening to a ledger that is not the repository's own means a receipt written into the real ledger can never carry a skipped blob check - the guard is on the thing the weakening could damage, not on the caller's intent.
designF3.where: immediately after resolveLedgerDir, before the evidence directory is used, before the first gh call and before any file is written or copied - so the refusal cannot leave a receipt or a copied review behind
designF3.comparison: on-disk identity: realpathSync.native on both sides, lowercased on win32, so a differently-cased or symlinked spelling of the same directory does not evade it
designF3.pinnedBy: a case that mirrors scripts/qc/{roadmap-unit-closure,roadmap-ledger-lib,preserve-run-logs}.mjs into a throwaway root whose openspec/planning/2026-09-12-roadmap-completion holds a stub units.json. The mirror makes that stub the module's OWN default ledger, so the guard is exercised on the same code path without the real ledger ever being the subject. The case asserts the refusal, and that the mirror's units.json is byte-unchanged and its evidence directory still empty.

designF2.finding: U17 F2: the Lane A reviewer model is the literal 'claude-sonnet (Agent model: sonnet)' in the closure, so a review by any other model would be receipted as sonnet.
designF2.chosen: read it from the Lane A review markdown's `reviewerModel:` header line, and refuse when the line is absent
designF2.whyNotAFlag: the charter of this unit names the header line. Every Lane A review already on main (u0, u1, u1b-e, u2, u3, u6, u7, u9, u9b, u11, u13, u14, u15b, u16, u17) carries `reviewerModel:` on its own line beside `reviewedHead:`, which the closure already parses out of the same file - so the value comes from the artefact being receipted rather than from a second argument the caller could contradict.
designF2.pinnedBy: a case whose seeded review names a model that is NOT the old literal, asserting both the review receipt and the unit entry carry the header's value; and a case whose review has no reviewerModel line, asserting the refusal and that no review receipt was written

designPreserveRunLogs.staged: preserveRunLogs is called after the mainProof receipt is written AND after its verdict is checked, so a FAIL closure refuses with the proof logs unpreserved
designPreserveRunLogs.chosen: move the call to immediately after the mainProof receipt is written and BEFORE the verdict refusal
designPreserveRunLogs.why: the module already records the run before refusing - the FAIL mainProof receipt is written and then the refusal is thrown - and the logs are part of that record. A FAIL is exactly the run whose logs are wanted, and DELIVERY.md's 'Owned cleanup' rule is about preserving evidence before a worktree is removed, not about the verdict. This resolves the limit the staging README recorded instead of carrying it forward as a non-claim.
designPreserveRunLogs.pinnedBy: the existing PASS case, strengthened to assert the manifest at evidence/u91-logs-20260917.json lists exactly the proof directory's own files; plus a new case asserting a FAIL closure still preserves them
